public.title: Mean By
public.description: Return the exact mean of the integer field key across rows as [sum, count], without reducing the fraction. Return null for no rows. Every row contains the selected key. Supported inputs contain at most 100 array entries per sequence and at most 20 operations or requests per sequence, at most 60 total object properties and array elements in any single JSON value, nesting depth at most 8, strings at most 100 ASCII characters unless specified otherwise, and integers from -100 through 100 unless a tighter or explicit alternate bound is stated. The entire argument JSON encoding is at most 1000 bytes. Nested sequences collectively have at most 100 entries; output snapshots therefore remain bounded. Inputs always satisfy the described shape and bounds.
hints: Keep numerator and denominator separately; do not round.
Check the public examples against the documented empty-input and boundary rules.
public.attribution: Original Bekor statement, examples, tests and reference code, 2026. Covers a common JavaScript practice topic; no third-party prose or code copied.

explanation: Accumulate selected fields, retaining row count as denominator. No division is needed and fractional means remain exact. O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space. This JSON adapter verifies observable results; it does not establish built-in-method restrictions, garbage collection, browser behavior or real timer/microtask scheduling.
